title: ElevenLabs Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits, and Costs
summary: ElevenLabs pricing structures rely on character counts rather than audio length to determine monthly costs. Readers can select the ideal subscription tier.
body_markdown:
## ElevenLabs pricing plans and character limits


### The credit system: How characters are consumed


Characters are the primary currency of the platform. The efficiency of your spend depends entirely on the model selected for the task.


> Every punctuation mark and space carries a literal price tag.


When using the high-fidelity Multilingual V2 model,[Sume](https://www.sume.com/blog/deepgram-aura-2-0-03-per-1000-characters-script-cost-vs-sume-tts) pays **$0.17 per 1,000 characters** . This is over ten times more expensive than[OpenAI TTS-1](https://www.sume.com/blog/deepgram-aura-2-0-03-per-1000-characters-script-cost-vs-sume-tts) at $0.015 per 1,000 characters.


Even the optimized ElevenLabs Flash model sits at $0.04 per 1,000 characters, a rate that exceeds the $0.03 offered by[Deepgram Aura-2](https://www.sume.com/blog/deepgram-aura-2-0-03-per-1000-characters-script-cost-vs-sume-tts) . Users pay a premium for the ElevenLabs brand.


The credit consumption follows a 1:1 ratio for standard models, where one character equals one credit.


The $0.17 figure represents a calculated breakdown of the total plan cost divided by the character allotment, meaning the effective price per unit is tied directly to the subscription tier.


This specific dollar value already accounts for the 2x multiplier applied to the Multilingual V2 model, so the user does not need to apply further adjustments when calculating their total spend.


A user reading a price list should not double this figure again, as the math reflects the final cost of the credits consumed by that specific engine.


The run is the meter for[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) , meaning a complex ten-step voice processing flow costs the same as a simple one-step trigger. Pricing that scales with every internal action effectively taxes a builder for the granularity required to manage ElevenLabs credits properly.


Because it charges **1 credit per flow run** regardless of the number of steps, users can add logic to check character counts or switch models without increasing their automation bill.


### ElevenLabs Free and Starter plans compared


ElevenLabs provides a Free plan with 10k credits per month for $0, allowing users to test the platform's capabilities without any financial commitment, so there is no barrier to entry for evaluating the voice quality.


This is only enough to generate about five minutes of audio.


Moving to the Starter plan costs $1 for the first month, 83% off the regular $6 price, meaning new subscribers can begin their integration with a very low initial financial commitment. This tier only grants 30,000 characters. A single long-form blog post can exhaust your entire monthly allotment in one click.


### Creator and Pro: The mid-tier sweet spots


Mid-range plans target consistent content creators who require commercial rights and higher throughput. The Creator plan at $22 per month offers 121,000 characters, providing a fixed capacity for users with moderate production needs, which ensures predictable monthly expenses for consistent workloads.


The Pro plan costs $99 for 600,000 characters, scaling the service to accommodate enterprise-level output requirements, thereby lowering the effective cost per unit for high-output operations.

### ElevenLabs Scale and Enterprise plan limits


1.8M characters are provided by the Scale plan for $299 per month, supporting roughly 25 hours of audio, so heavy users can process extensive amounts of content without needing to purchase additional blocks. The Scale tier has the highest standard capacity.


On Enterprise plans, custom quotas and volume-based discounts are the only way to access those features. Teams exceeding two million characters monthly must negotiate direct contracts to avoid prohibitive overage fees.
